claim: Image3C is a multimodal image-based and label-independent integrative method for single-cell analysis.
source: Image3C, a multimodal image-based and label-independent integrative method for single-cell analysis
evidence: The title directly states the nature and purpose of Image3C as described in the manuscript.

claim: Image-based cell classification has become a common tool to identify phenotypic changes in cell populations.
source: Image-based cell classification has become a common tool to identify phenotypic changes in cell populations.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact in the abstract.

claim: Image-based classification methodology is limited to organisms possessing well-characterized species-specific reagents (e.g., antibodies) that allow cell identification, clustering, and convolutional neural network (CNN) training.
source: However, this methodology is limited to organisms possessing well-characterized species-specific reagents (e.g., antibodies) that allow cell identification, clustering, and convolutional neural network (CNN) training.
evidence: This limitation is explicitly stated in the abstract as context for the development of Image3C.

claim: Image3C does not require species-specific reagents nor pre-existing knowledge about the sample.
source: We have developed an image-based classification methodology we named Image3C (Image-Cytometry Cell Classification) that does not require species-specific reagents nor pre-existing knowledge about the sample.
evidence: This is a core claim about the capabilities of Image3C stated in the abstract.

claim: Image3C combines image-based flow cytometry with an unbiased, high-throughput cell clustering pipeline and CNN integration.
source: Image3C combines image-based flow cytometry with an unbiased, high-throughput cell clustering pipeline and CNN integration.
evidence: This describes the technical components of the Image3C method as stated in the abstract.

claim: Image3C exploits intrinsic cellular features and non-species-specific dyes to perform de novo cell composition analysis and detect changes between different conditions.
source: Image3C exploits intrinsic cellular features and non-species-specific dyes to perform de novo cell composition analysis and detect changes between different conditions.
evidence: This describes the approach used by Image3C as stated in the abstract.

claim: Image3C expands the use of image-based analyses of cell population composition to research organisms in which detailed cellular phenotypes are unknown or for which species-specific reagents are not available.
source: Therefore, Image3C expands the use of image-based analyses of cell population composition to research organisms in which detailed cellular phenotypes are unknown or for which species-specific reagents are not available.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract about the applicability of Image3C.

claim: Single-cell analysis has proven crucial to understanding fundamental biological processes such as development, homeostasis, regeneration, aging, and disease.
source: Single-cell analysis has proven crucial to our understanding of fundamental biological processes such as development, homeostasis, regeneration, aging, and disease (Goolam et al., 2016; Kimmel et al., 2019; Pepe-Mooney et al., 2019; Philippeos et al., 2018; Tirosh et al., 2016).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: Recent advances in image-based cell profiling and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) allow quantification of differences between cell populations and comparisons of cell type composition between samples.
source: Recent advances in image-based cell profiling and single-cell RNA sequencing (scRNA-seq) allow quantification of differences between cell populations and comparisons of cell type composition between samples (Caicedo et al., 2017).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation to published work.

claim: Single-cell studies that use traditional research organisms (e.g., mouse, rat, or fruit fly) benefit from the availability of genomic platforms and established antibody libraries.
source: Single-cell studies that use traditional research organisms (e.g., mouse, rat, or fruit fly) benefit from the availability of genomic platforms and established antibody libraries.
evidence: This is stated as an established fact about traditional model organisms.

claim: The successful identification and enumeration of biologically meaningful cell types can be harmed by both the limited number and variety of cellular attributes available for determination of cell types and by observer bias when using traditional, hand-counting approaches.
source: Yet, the successful identification and enumeration of biologically meaningful cell types in such studies can be harmed by both the limited number and variety of cellular attributes (few features or low dynamic range) available for determination of cell types and by observer bias when using traditional, hand-counting approaches (e.g., hemocytometer and Giemsa stain) (van der Meer et al., 2004).
evidence: This claim is supported by a citation and describes limitations of traditional methods.

claim: Automated classification of cells using convolutional neural networks (CNNs) has become a promising approach for accurate high-throughput cell analysis that is free from observer bias.
source: Automated classification of cells using convolutional neural networks (CNNs, machine learning [ML] method specialized in image recognition and classification) has become a promising approach for accurate high-throughput cell analysis that is free from observer bias (Blasi et al., 2016; Eulenberg et al., 2017; Kobayashi et al., 2017; Lei et al., 2018; Nassar et al., 2019; Suzuki et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations to published literature.

claim: CNN-based automated clustering and classification techniques require pre-existing knowledge about the organism or cell type of interest or the availability of cell-specific reagents or genomic sequence.
source: To date, CNN-based automated clustering and classification techniques require pre-existing knowledge about the organism or cell type of interest (e.g., cell-specific morphological traits within an image set) or the availability of cell-specific reagents (e.g., antibodies), or genomic sequence (e.g., single-cell sequencing) (Table 1 shows an overview of the existing methods) (Baron et al., 2019; Blasi et al., 2016; Cheng et al., 2021; Eulenberg et al., 2017; Hennig et al., 2017; Kobayashi et al., 2017; Lei et al., 2018; Nassar et al., 2019).
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple citations and reference to Table 1.

claim: Image3C was tested on zebrafish whole kidney marrow and apple snail hemolymph.
source: Image3C (present work)	YES (Zebrafish whole kidney marrow; Apple snail hemolymph)
evidence: Table 1 explicitly lists the cell types tested with Image3C.

claim: Image3C does not require previous knowledge or species-specific reagents to cluster cell images and train the neural network.
source: NO Does not require previous knowledge or species-specific reagents to cluster cell images and train the neural network. If available, they can be used/integrated.
evidence: Table 1 explicitly states this characteristic of Image3C.

claim: Image3C uses commercially available hardware (ImageStream).
source: YES (ImageStream)
evidence: Table 1 explicitly states the hardware used by Image3C.

claim: Image3C uses free or open source software including IDEAS, Vortex, R, and Python.
source: YES (IDEAS; Vortex; R; Python) NO (FCS Express Plus)
evidence: Table 1 explicitly lists the software used by Image3C.

claim: CellProfiler requires annotated datasets to train the machine learning algorithms, either by staining the samples with known markers, or by manually clustering the cells.
source: YES Requires annotated datasets to train the machine learning algorithms, either by staining the samples with known markers, or by manually clustering the cells.
evidence: Table 1 explicitly describes the requirements of CellProfiler.

claim: CellProfiler Analyst requires the use of fluorescent markers to annotate the cells and use them as the ground truth to train the machine learning algorithms.
source: YES Requires the use of fluorescent markers to annotate the cells and use them as the ground truth to train the machine learning algorithms.
evidence: Table 1 explicitly describes the requirements of CellProfiler Analyst.

claim: Label-free reflectance microscopy requires immunofluorescence images with known markers to use as ground truth and for training multiple deep learning models.
source: YES Requires immunofluorescence images with known markers to use as ground truth and for training multiple deep learning models.
evidence: Table 1 explicitly describes the requirements of label-free reflectance microscopy.

claim: Optofluidic time-stretch microscopy does not provide cell clustering and single-cell resolution analysis.
source: YES Does not provide cell clustering and single-cell resolution analysis. The changes are analyzed overall in the sample without assigning it to a cell type.
evidence: Table 1 explicitly describes the limitations of optofluidic time-stretch microscopy.

claim: Raman scattering requires homogenous cell cultures that after different treatments are used to create databases for training deep learning models.
source: YES Requires homogenous cell cultures. After different treatments, these samples are used to create databases for training deep learning models.
evidence: Table 1 explicitly describes the requirements of Raman scattering methods.

claim: Fluorescence lifetime imaging depends on other techniques to identify cell types to compare their autofluorescence signals and fluorescence decay for further analysis.
source: YES Depends on other techniques to identify cell types to compare their autofluorescence signals and fluorescence decay for further analysis.
evidence: Table 1 explicitly describes the requirements of fluorescence lifetime imaging.

claim: Image3C can identify different cell populations based on morphology and/or function through de novo clustering.
source: We demonstrated that Image3C can identify different cell populations based on morphology and/or function through de novo clustering and highlight important changes in cell type abundance and cell population composition caused by experimental or natural perturbation (sex, treatment, experimental protocol).
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated capability in the Conclusion section.

claim: Image3C can highlight important changes in cell type abundance and cell population composition caused by experimental or natural perturbation (sex, treatment, experimental protocol).
source: We demonstrated that Image3C can identify different cell populations based on morphology and/or function through de novo clustering and highlight important changes in cell type abundance and cell population composition caused by experimental or natural perturbation (sex, treatment, experimental protocol).
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated capability in the Conclusion section.

claim: Image3C in combination with the CNN classifier is capable of bias-free and high-throughput analysis of large experimental datasets.
source: Furthermore, in combination with the CNN classifier trained on these clusters, we demonstrate that Image3C is capable of bias-free and high-throughput analysis of large experimental datasets making it possible to compare a specific cell type behavior or population composition across multiple experiments.
evidence: This is stated as a demonstrated capability in the Conclusion section.

claim: Image3C is extremely versatile and can be applied to any tissue or cell population of interest and is adaptable to a variety of experimental designs.
source: Image3C is extremely versatile and can be applied to any tissue or cell population of interest and is adaptable to a variety of experimental designs.
evidence: This is stated as a conclusion about the versatility of Image3C.

claim: Image3C identified 16 clusters in zebrafish whole kidney marrow (WKM) tissue based on intrinsic morphological and fluorescent features.
source: Clustering by the final set of normalized and non-redundant morphological and fluorescent features produced distinct cell populations (Figure 2A–C, Figure 2—figure supplements 1–3).
evidence: Figure 2A shows 16 distinct clusters identified in zebrafish WKM tissue.

claim: Image3C can distinguish between the major classes of cells present in zebrafish WKM.
source: Image3C can distinguish between the major classes of cells present in zebrafish WKM (Figure 2; Supplementary files 3 and 4) that were described using standard sorting flow cytometry and morphological staining approaches (Traver et al., 2003).
evidence: This claim is supported by comparison with published methods and data shown in Figure 2.

claim: Image3C can clearly identify dead cells and debris.
source: It is noteworthy that Image3C can clearly identify dead cells and debris (Figure 2A, B) allowing to optimize experimental protocols in order to minimize cell death and run the subsequent analysis only on the intact, live cells.
evidence: This capability is explicitly stated and shown in Figure 2.

claim: Image3C can identify cells with outstanding morphological features, such as neutrophils from other myelomonocytes.
source: Image3C can identify cells with outstanding morphological features, such as neutrophils from other myelomonocytes (Figure 2B, C).
evidence: This capability is explicitly stated and shown in Figure 2.

claim: The myelomonocyte to lymphocyte ratio obtained with Image3C (M/L ratio = 1.59) is similar to the one obtained with classic histological approaches (mean M/L ratio = 1.35).
source: Although a direct comparison with results from classical approaches (Traver et al., 2003) is not possible since we gated out (removed analytically) mature erythrocytes before clustering (Materials and methods), the myelomonocyte to lymphocyte ratio (M/L ratio = 1.59) is similar to the one obtained with classic histological approaches (mean M/L ratio = 1.35) (Figure 2D; Traver et al., 2003).
evidence: This comparison is explicitly stated with specific numerical values and supported by citation.

claim: Image3C identified 4 clusters of professional phagocytes in zebrafish WKM: granulocytes within clusters Dr4_P, Dr12_P, and Dr13_P and monocytic cells in cluster Dr21_P.
source: Visualizing these clustered event images (Supplementary file 7) while considering the values and intensities of their morphological and fluorescent features (Supplementary file 3) allowed identification of 4 clusters of professional phagocytes: granulocytes within clusters Dr4_P, Dr12_P, and Dr13_P and monocytic cells in cluster Dr21_P (Figure 3A, B).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and shown in Figure 3.

claim: The relative abundance of professional phagocytes in zebrafish WKM is 5–10%, which is in line with previous studies using classical morphological approaches.
source: Overall, the relative abundance of professional phagocytes is 5–10% (Figure 3C), which is in line with previous studies that estimated the number of professional phagocytes in WKM tissue of adult zebrafish using classical morphological approaches (Wittamer et al., 2011).
evidence: This claim is supported by data shown in Figure 3C and comparison with published literature.

claim: Image3C did not observe a cluster of lymphocytes (e.g., B-cells) that actively phagocytize CTV-S. aureus bacteria in zebrafish WKM.
source: It is also noteworthy that in line with other studies (Page et al., 2013) we did not observe a cluster of lymphocytes (e.g., B-cells) that actively phagocytize CTV-S. aureus bacteria (Figure 2; Supplementary file 7).
evidence: This observation is explicitly stated and supported by citation to published work.

claim: CCB selectively affects cell viability based on cell identity, introducing artifacts and cell damage, actions not specific to inhibition of phagocytosis.
source: A new aspect that Image3C highlighted is that CCB selectively affects cell viability based on cell identity, introducing artifacts and cell damage, actions not specific to inhibition of phagocytosis (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a new finding revealed by Image3C analysis as shown in Figure 3B.

claim: All mature erythrocyte-containing clusters had a significantly higher cell count in the CTV-S. aureus samples compared to the CTV-S. aureus + CCB ones.
source: All mature erythrocyte-containing clusters had a significantly higher cell count in the CTV-S. aureus samples compared to the CTV-S. aureus + CCB ones (Figure 3B; Supplementary files 3 and 5).
evidence: This observation is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 3B and supplementary files.

claim: Erythrocytes were almost absent in samples incubated with CCB.
source: Cluster analysis revealed that erythrocytes were almost absent in samples incubated with CCB (Supplementary file 3), while there was a significant increase in the relative abundance of clusters containing dead and apoptotic cells (Figure 3B; Supplementary file 5).
evidence: This observation is explicitly stated and supported by data.

claim: The inhibition of phagocytosis through low temperature only affects adhesive neutrophils (cluster Dr12_P).
source: This is suspected to occur as ice inhibits adhesion, while CCB effectively blocks phagocytosis in all professional phagocytes in zebrafish WKM tissue by acting on the cytoskeleton. The use of Image3C allowed us to specifically identify cell types that are sensible to low temperature and those that are not, confirming the existence of different phagocytosis mechanisms and providing additional knowledge about pros and cons of different protocols that can be applied to inhibit phagocytosis based on specific goals and needs.
evidence: This observation is explicitly stated based on Image3C analysis comparing different inhibition methods.

claim: Image3C identified 9 cell clusters in P. canaliculata hemolymph in homeostasis conditions.
source: We used Image3C to analyze the images of the events and identified 9 cell clusters (Figure 4A, Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is explicitly stated and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: The clusters obtained by Image3C for P. canaliculata hemocytes were consistent with published P. canaliculata hemocyte classification obtained by classical morphological methods.
source: The clusters obtained by Image3C were not only homogeneous and biologically meaningful but were also consistent with published P. canaliculata hemocyte classification obtained by classical morphological methods (Accorsi et al., 2013).
evidence: This consistency is explicitly stated and supported by citation.

claim: The relative abundance of small blast-like cells in P. canaliculata hemolymph is 14.0% by traditional methods and 13.8% by Image3C (cluster Pc4).
source: For example, the relative abundance of the previously reported small blast-like cells is 14.0%, a value almost identical to the abundance of the corresponding cluster Pc4 (13.8%).
evidence: This comparison is explicitly stated with specific numerical values.

claim: The category of larger hemocytes or Group II hemocytes represents 80.4% of the circulating cells by traditional morphological methods, while clusters Pc1, Pc6, Pc7, and Pc9 combined represent 72.4% of the events analyzed with Image3C.
source: Similarly, the category of larger hemocytes or Group II hemocytes represents 80.4% of the circulating cells as measured by traditional morphological methods, while clusters Pc1, Pc6, Pc7, and Pc9 combined represent 72.4% of the events analyzed with Image3C (Figure 4C; Supplementary file 3).
evidence: This comparison is explicitly stated with specific numerical values.

claim: Granular cells (cluster Pc6) correspond to 7.7% of all hemocytes by classical histological methods and 8.9% by Image3C.
source: A subset of these cells are the granular cells (cluster Pc6), which correspond to 7.7% of all hemocytes by classical histological methods and 8.9% by Image3C.
evidence: This comparison is explicitly stated with specific numerical values.

claim: Image3C represents an unprecedented increase in the accuracy of cell type identification over traditional histological methods, while also allowing high-throughput capability.
source: Hence, Image3C not only can properly analyze cells obtained from an emerging research organism generating biologically meaningful and informative clusters but also represents an unprecedented increase in the accuracy of cell type identification over traditional histological methods, while also allowing high-throughput capability.
evidence: This conclusion is explicitly stated based on the comparison with traditional methods.

claim: Image3C identified two clusters enriched with professional phagocytes in P. canaliculata hemolymph (cluster Pc5_P and Pc17_P).
source: The clusters with relative abundance significantly higher in the phagocytosis samples (Figure 5B; Supplementary files 3 and 11) and with high intensities of both DHR and bacteria signals (Figure 5—figure supplements 3 and 4) are the two clusters that we identify as enriched with professional phagocyte (cluster Pc5_P and Pc17_P) (Figure 5B, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 5—figure supplement 4; Supplementary file 11).
evidence: This identification is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 5.

claim: The two professional phagocyte clusters in P. canaliculata (Pc5_P and Pc17_P) show different DHR signal intensity (ROS response) from one another upon bacteria exposure.
source: The two clusters show a different DHR signal intensity (ROS response) from one another upon bacteria exposure (cluster Pc5_P with high DHR signal, cluster Pc17_P with low DHR signal) (Figure 5—figure supplement 3; Supplementary files 3 and 11).
evidence: This observation is explicitly stated and supported by data in supplementary figures.

claim: EDTA effectively inhibits phagocytosis for both types of professional phagocytes in P. canaliculata.
source: Both Pc5_P and Pc17_P relative abundance is significantly higher in the phagocytosis samples compared to the EDTA-treated sample (Figure 5C; Supplementary file 9), showing that EDTA effectively inhibits phagocytosis for both types of professional phagocytes.
evidence: This conclusion is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 5C.

claim: In P. canaliculata, only cluster Pc17_P had a significantly lower relative abundance in the ice-inhibited phagocytosis sample compared to the phagocytosis sample.
source: In the sample where the phagocytosis was inhibited by low temperature, however, only cluster Pc17_P had a significantly lower relative abundance compared to the phagocytosis sample (Figure 5C, Figure 3—figure supplement 2; Supplementary file 10).
evidence: This observation is explicitly stated and supported by data in Figure 5C.

claim: EDTA is a more effective and generalized (not cell type-specific) inhibitor of phagocytosis than low temperature in P. canaliculata.
source: We can conclude that similar to CCB inhibition in the zebrafish phagocytosis experiment, EDTA is a more effective and generalized (not cell type-specific) inhibitor of phagocytosis than low temperature.
evidence: This conclusion is explicitly stated based on the comparison of inhibition methods.

claim: The CNN classifier was trained using over 35,000 images of P. canaliculata hemolymph cell types in homeostasis condition.
source: The CNN was used to train a classifier using over 35,000 images of P. canaliculata hemolymph cell types in homeostasis condition acquired with the ImageStreamX Mark II system.
evidence: This is explicitly stated in the methods section describing CNN training.

claim: The weighted average precision score (f1-score) of the trained CNN classifier is 0.75.
source: The weighted average precision score (f1-score, precision average score across clusters controlling for support numbers) of 0.75 is relatively high considering the complexity of the phenotype (brightfield [BF], darkfield, and Draq5 images) (Figure 6D) and comparable to other studies using ML for cell classification (Blasi et al., 2016).
evidence: This performance metric is explicitly stated and compared to other studies.

claim: 59.4% of the phagocytes in P. canaliculata belonged to cluster Pc1_CT, 6.2% to Pc6_CT, and 9.2% to Pc7_CT.
source: We found that 59.4, 6.2, and 9.2% of the phagocytes belonged to cluster Pc1_CT, Pc6_CT, and Pc7_CT, respectively (Figure 6E), where CT stands for classifier training.
evidence: These specific percentages are explicitly stated and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: The hemocytes able to phagocytize in P. canaliculata were primarily Group II hemocytes, confirming previously published results using classical morphological staining and manual annotation.
source: These results confirmed a previously published result that used classical morphological staining and manual annotation to conclude that the hemocytes able to phagocytize were primarily Group II hemocytes (Accorsi et al., 2013).
evidence: This confirmation is explicitly stated and supported by citation.

claim: Only 8% of the phagocytes in P. canaliculata were clustered in the Group I hemocytes (clusters Pc2_CT, Pc3_CT, and Pc4_CT).
source: Only 8% of the phagocytes were clustered in the Group I hemocytes, here represented by clusters Pc2_CT, Pc3_CT, and Pc4_CT, while the remaining 17.2% were assigned by the CNN to the cluster Pc5_CT, constituted by doublets and dead cells (Figure 6E).
evidence: This percentage is explicitly stated and shown in Figure 6E.

claim: In vitro phagocytosis triggers microaggregate formation (hemocyte-hemocyte adhesion) in invertebrate hemocytes that resembles the nodule formation observed in vivo.
source: This result can be explained by the fact that in vitro phagocytosis triggers microaggregate formation (hemocyte-hemocyte adhesion) in invertebrate hemocytes that resembles the nodule formation observed in vivo (Walters, 1970).
evidence: This explanation is explicitly stated and supported by citation.

claim: The comparison between female and male P. canaliculata hemocyte compositions revealed that clusters Pc1_CT, Pc7_CT, and Pc6_CT are significantly different in terms of relative abundance.
source: The comparison between female and male hemocyte compositions revealed that the clusters significantly different in terms of relative abundance are Pc1_CT and Pc7_CT (Group II agranular large hemocytes) and Pc6_CT (Group II granular large hemocytes) (Figure 6F).
evidence: This comparison is explicitly stated and shown in Figure 6F.

claim: One of the two subpopulations of agranular large hemocytes (Pc1_CT) was significantly more abundant in female P. canaliculata animals (53%) compared to males (38%).
source: The reduced user bias and high-throughput analysis presented here, in contrast, allowed us to determine that one of the two subpopulations of agranular large hemocytes was significantly more abundant in the female animals (Pc1_CT: 53 and 38% in females and males, respectively) while the other agranular (Pc7_CT) as well as the granular large hemocytes (Pc6_CT) was significantly more abundant in the male animals (Pc7_CT: 14 and 20% in females and males, respectively; Pc6_CT: 6 and 10% in females and males, respectively) (Figure 6F).
evidence: These specific percentages are explicitly stated and shown in Figure 6F.

claim: Prior studies detected no differences between female and male P. canaliculata hemocyte composition through manual classification and counting using a classical morphological approach.
source: Significantly, prior studies detected no differences between females and males hemocytes composition through manual classification and counting using a classical morphological approach (Accorsi et al., 2013).
evidence: This comparison with prior studies is explicitly stated and supported by citation.

claim: Image3C does not require initial antibody staining.
source: In comparison to existing label-free cell clustering methods, Image3C does not require initial antibody staining (Cheng et al., 2021; Hennig et al., 2017; Lippeveld et al., 2020; Nassar et al., 2019), pre-existing knowledge of specific cell morphology (Suzuki et al., 2019; Yakimov et al., 2019), and is not limited to a specific cellular phenotype (Blasi et al., 2016) for a priori identification of certain cell types (Table 1).
evidence: This advantage is explicitly stated and supported by citations to other methods.

claim: Image3C does not require pre-existing knowledge of specific cell morphology.
source: In comparison to existing label-free cell clustering methods, Image3C does not require initial antibody staining (Cheng et al., 2021; Hennig et al., 2017; Lippeveld et al., 2020; Nassar et al., 2019), pre-existing knowledge of specific cell morphology (Suzuki et al., 2019; Yakimov et al., 2019), and is not limited to a specific cellular phenotype (Blasi et al., 2016) for a priori identification of certain cell types (Table 1).
evidence: This advantage is explicitly stated and supported by citations to other methods.

claim: Image3C is not limited to a specific cellular phenotype for a priori identification of certain cell types.
source: In comparison to existing label-free cell clustering methods, Image3C does not require initial antibody staining (Cheng et al., 2021; Hennig et al., 2017; Lippeveld et al., 2020; Nassar et al., 2019), pre-existing knowledge of specific cell morphology (Suzuki et al., 2019; Yakimov et al., 2019), and is not limited to a specific cellular phenotype (Blasi et al., 2016) for a priori identification of certain cell types (Table 1).
evidence: This advantage is explicitly stated and supported by citations to other methods.

claim: Image3C can take advantage of species-specific reagents and prior knowledge to be combined with transcriptomic datasets and provide a new and complementary layer of information based on cell morphology and function.
source: Parallelly to this de novo clustering approach, Image3C can take advantage of species-specific reagents and prior knowledge to be combined with transcriptomic dataset and provide a new and complimentary layer of information based on cell morphology and function.
evidence: This capability is explicitly stated as an additional feature of Image3C.

claim: Image3C combines modern high-throughput data acquisition by image-based flow cytometry, advanced and unbiased clustering analysis, statistics to compare cellular compositions across different samples, and a CNN classifier component.
source: In sum, Image3C combines modern high-throughput data acquisition by image-based flow cytometry, advanced and unbiased clustering analysis, statistics to compare cellular compositions across different samples, and a CNN classifier component to easily determine changes in cell composition across multiple experiments.
evidence: This summary of Image3C components is explicitly stated.

claim: The number of clusters drastically increases when including treatments that influence cell morphological properties of the cell.
source: In addition, we observed that the number of clusters drastically increases when including treatments that influence cell morphological properties of the cell. As an example, while we detected 9 unique clusters in naïve hemolymph samples, we detected 20 clusters in the phagocytosis experiment (Figure 3A, Figure 4A).
evidence: This observation is explicitly stated with specific examples from the data.

claim: Professional phagocytes change their morphology upon detection of pathogens.
source: This is in part due to the fact that professional phagocytes change their morphology upon detection of pathogens (Palić et al., 2007), thus creating new clusters.
evidence: This explanation is explicitly stated and supported by citation.

claim: The ImageStreamX Mark II system provides highly reproducible and comparable images of cells coming from different experiments and acquired at different days.
source: A crucial element that allows this approach is also represented by the ImageStreamX Mark II system that provides highly reproducible and comparable images of cells coming from different experiments and acquired at different days, introducing much less variability than standard light or electron microscopy.
evidence: This characteristic of the ImageStreamX Mark II system is explicitly stated.

claim: The CNN used in Image3C is based on the architecture of DenseNet.
source: For our pipeline, then, a CNN (LeCun et al., 1989) based on the architecture of DenseNet (Huang et al., 2017) was deployed to (1) use, as training set, images and clusters obtained from a first group of samples (e.g., homeostasis conditions, naïve cells, or WT samples) analyzed in an unbiased way by de novo clustering and (2) assign new cell images acquired through ImageStreamX Mark II system to their respective classes.
evidence: This technical detail is explicitly stated with citations.

claim: The CNN consists of three dense blocks that transition from three-channel image input of 32 × 32 × 3 to a final size of 4 × 4 × 87 with 87 feature maps.
source: The CNN consists of three dense blocks that transition from three-channel image input of 32 × 32 × 3 to a final size of 4 × 4 × 87 with 87 feature maps.
evidence: This technical specification of the CNN architecture is explicitly stated.

claim: The CNN used softmax cross-entropy for the loss function with L2 regularization, and the Adam optimizer was used to minimize the loss function.
source: The CNN used softmax cross-entropy for the loss function with L2 regularization, and the Adam optimizer (Kingma and Ba, 2014) was used to minimize the loss function.
evidence: This technical detail about the CNN training is explicitly stated with citation.

claim: The CNN was implemented in Python using the TensorFlow platform and the SciPy ecosystem.
source: The CNN was implemented in Python using the TensorFlow platform (Abadi et al., 2015) and the SciPy ecosystem (Oliphant, 2006; Oliphant, 2007; Pedregosa et al., 2011).
evidence: This implementation detail is explicitly stated with citations.

claim: The training proceeded for 25,000 iterations with a size of 256 randomly selected images for each iteration.
source: The training proceeded for 25,000 iterations with a size of 256 randomly selected images for each iteration.
evidence: This training parameter is explicitly stated.

claim: The training and test sets follow the same accuracy and loss trends over all iterations, indicating the training set is not memorized and can generalize to predict the test set.
source: The training and test sets follow the same accuracy and loss trends over all iterations, indicating the training set is not memorized and can generalize to predict the test set.
evidence: This conclusion about the CNN training is explicitly stated.

claim: X-Shift was selected as a clustering method for Image3C based on a previously published analysis and comparison of clustering methods.
source: X-Shift was selected as a clustering method for Image3C based on a previously published analysis and comparison of clustering methods (Weber and Robinson, 2016).
evidence: This methodological choice is explicitly stated and supported by citation.

claim: X-shift represents an optimal trade-off: identifying low-frequency populations, accurately identifying 'true' clusters (i.e., F1 scores), not requiring a priori knowledge of the number of clusters (populations) and having reasonable runtimes.
source: From that work, we determined that X-shift represents an optimal trade-off: identifying low-frequency populations, accurately identifying 'true' clusters (i.e., F1 scores), not requiring for a priori knowledge of the number of clusters (populations) and having reasonable runtimes (due to hardware CPU requirements).
evidence: This justification for choosing X-shift is explicitly stated.

claim: K-means was insufficient for Image3C purposes as known cell populations were not well represented by clusters, and the method requires specification of the number of expected clusters.
source: We also did an early comparison of X-shift with K-means (data not shown) and determined that K-means was insufficient for our purposes as known cell populations were not well represented by clusters, and we did not want to specify the number of expected clusters into the method's input parameters since this would not be known in experimental use.
evidence: This comparison and justification is explicitly stated.

claim: Negative binomial regression was performed on tables of cell counts per cluster and per sample using R with the edgeR package.
source: Negative binomial regression was performed on tables of cell counts per cluster and per sample and plots were generated using R (R Development Core Team, 2014) with the edgeR package (Robinson et al., 2010), which was developed for RNA-seq analysis, but includes generally applicable and user-friendly wrappers for regression, modeling analysis, and plotting of results.
evidence: This statistical method is explicitly stated with citations.

claim: For the comparison of cellular hemolymph composition between females and males of P. canaliculata, a one-way ANOVA with subsequent FDR (Benjamini–Hochberg, correction for multiple testing) was used.
source: For the comparison of cellular hemolymph composition between females and males of P. canaliculata, a one-way ANOVA with subsequent FDR (Benjamini–Hochberg, correction for multiple testing) was used.
evidence: This statistical method is explicitly stated.

claim: Twelve-month-old, wild type, female, adult zebrafish were used for WKM collection.
source: Twelve-month-old, wild type, female, adult zebrafish were euthanized with cold 500 mg/L MS-222 solution for 5 min.
evidence: This experimental detail is explicitly stated in the methods.

claim: Wild-type adult P. canaliculata snails, 7–9 months old and with a shell size of 45–60 mm, were starved for 5 days before the hemolymph collection.
source: Wild-type adult snails, 7–9 months old and with a shell size of 45–60 mm, were starved for 5 days before the hemolymph collection (Accorsi et al., 2013).
evidence: This experimental detail is explicitly stated in the methods with citation.

claim: For zebrafish WKM morphology assay, 10,000 nucleated and focused events were recorded for each sample (n = 8).
source: Cells were stained with 5 µM Draq5 (Thermo Fisher Scientific) for 10 min and subsequently run on the ImageStreamX Mark II (Amnis Millipore Sigma), where 10,000 nucleated and focused events were recorded for each sample (n = 8).
evidence: This experimental detail is explicitly stated in the methods.

claim: Erythrocytes were outgated to enrich for immune-relevant cells and prevent overclustering in the subsequent analysis.
source: Erythrocytes were outgated to enrich for immune-relevant cells and prevent overclustering in the subsequent analysis. The latter is due to the fact that fish erythrocytes are nucleated and their biconcave shape results in different morphological feature values only depending on their orientation during image acquisition.
evidence: This methodological choice is explicitly stated with justification.

claim: For P. canaliculata hemocyte morphology assay, 10,000 nucleated and focused events were imaged for each sample (n = 5).
source: The P. canaliculata hemocytes were stained with 5 µM Draq5 for 10 min, moved to ice, and subsequently run on the ImageStreamX Mark II, where 10,000 nucleated and focused events were imaged for each sample (n = 5).
evidence: This experimental detail is explicitly stated in the methods.

claim: Staphylococcus aureus were resuspended in PBS at the final concentration of 100 mg/mL and incubated with 5 µM CTV for 20 min.
source: Staphylococcus aureus (Thermo Fisher Scientific) were resuspended in PBS at the final concentration of 100 mg/mL and incubated with 5 µM CTV (Thermo Fisher Scientific) for 20 min.
evidence: This experimental protocol detail is explicitly stated in the methods.

claim: Cells were plated at a concentration of 4 × 10^5 cells/well in 200 µL of medium and incubated with 2 × 10^7 CTV-coupled S. aureus/well for 3 h at room temperature for the phagocytosis assay.
source: Cells, obtained from fish WKM or snail hemolymph and in a single cell suspension, were plated in a 96-well plate at a concentration of 4 × 105 cells/well in 200 µL of medium and incubated with 2 × 107 CTV-coupled S. aureus/well for 3 h at room temperature.
evidence: This experimental protocol detail is explicitly stated in the methods.

claim: Phagocytosis was inhibited by incubating cells with CTV-S. aureus either on ice or with 0.08 mg/mL CCB for zebrafish cells or with 30 mM EDTA and 10 mM HEPES for apple snail cells.
source: As control, the phagocytosis was inhibited incubating the cells + CTV-S. aureus mix either on ice (for both species) or with 0.08 mg/mL CCB for zebrafish cells or with 30 mM EDTA and 10 mM HEPES for apple snail cells (Cueto et al., 2015; Li et al., 2006).
evidence: This experimental protocol detail is explicitly stated in the methods with citations.

claim: 5 µM DHR was added to the cell suspension after 2 h and 30 min to stain cells positive for ROS production.
source: After 2 h and 30 min, we added 5 µM DHR (Thermo Fisher Scientific) to the cell suspension to stain cells positive for ROS production.
evidence: This experimental protocol detail is explicitly stated in the methods.

claim: Data were acquired from each sample on the ImageStreamX Mark II at 60× magnification, slow/sensitive flow speed (1,000 images/s), using 633, 488, and 405 nm laser excitation.
source: Following cell preparation, data were acquired from each sample on the ImageStreamX Mark II at 60× magnification, slow/sensitive flow speed (1,000 images/s), using 633, 488, and 405 nm laser excitation.
evidence: This data acquisition detail is explicitly stated in the methods.

claim: Spearman's correlation values for each pair of features were calculated and one of the features of the pair was trimmed when correlation between the two was ≥0.85.
source: In order to trim redundant features that contribute noise but little new information, Spearman's correlation values for each pair of features were calculated using all events of a representative sample and one of the features of the pair was trimmed when correlation between the two was ≥0.85 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1; Caicedo et al., 2017).
evidence: This data processing detail is explicitly stated in the methods with citation.

claim: Samples with correlation of mean feature values below 0.85 with the set were discarded as outliers.
source: The Spearman's correlation of the mean values of remaining features per each sample was then used to identify outliers among sample replicates. Samples with correlation of mean feature values below 0.85 with the set were discarded (Figure 2—figure supplement 2, Figure 3—figure supplement 1, Figure 4—figure supplement 1, Figure 5—figure supplement 1), although in general the replicates were consistent.
evidence: This data processing detail is explicitly stated in the methods.

source: Also, while morphological features did not require any transformation or normalization, fluorescence intensity features were transformed using the estimateLogicle() and transform() functions from the R flowCore package (Ellis et al., 2018; Hahne et al., 2009) to improve homoscedasticity (homogeneity of variance) of distributions.
evidence: This data processing detail is explicitly stated in the methods with citations.

evidence: This data processing detail is explicitly stated in the methods with citation.

source: During the import into VorteX, all features were scaled to 1 SD to equalize the contribution of features towards clustering.
evidence: This data processing detail is explicitly stated in the methods.

source: Clustering was performed in VorteX testing a range of k values (typically from 5 to 150), choosing a final k value using the 'find elbow point for cluster number' function in VorteX and confirming visually that over- or underclustering did not occur.
